text: Oceans hold about 1.3 billion cubic kilometres of water
as_written: about 1.3 billion cubic kilometres of water
source: USGS Water Science School, 'How much water is there on Earth?'

text: Oceans hold 96.5 percent of Earth's water
as_written: 96.5 percent of all the water on Earth
source: USGS Water Science School

text: Oceans cover about 71 percent of Earth's surface
source: NOAA National Ocean Service

text: The continental shelf edge lies at roughly 130 metres depth on average
source: NOAA National Ocean Service, continental shelf; global shelf-break compilations

text: Average ocean depth is about 3.7 kilometres
source: NOAA / NCEI ETOPO global relief model

text: The Grand Canyon is about 1.8 kilometres deep at its deepest
source: US National Park Service, Grand Canyon (about 6,000 feet maximum depth)

text: Mauna Kea measured from its seafloor base is over 10 kilometres tall
source: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory

text: Everest is 8,849 metres tall
source: 2020 joint Nepal and China survey

text: The mid-ocean ridge is about 65,000 km long
source: NOAA Ocean Exploration

text: The Mariana Trench floor is nearly 11 km below sea level
as_written: nearly 11 kilometres below the old sea surface
source: Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping, University of New Hampshire; Five Deeps Expedition 2019

text: Everest's summit would sit over 2 km below sea level if placed in the trench (11 km minus 8.849 km)
as_written: over two kilometres below where the waves used to be
source: Arithmetic from the trench depth and Everest height cited above

text: With the oceans removed, atmospheric pressure at the old coastline would fall by roughly a quarter, equal to about 2.5 km altitude. This is a rough hydrostatic estimate, not a published result.
as_written: it drops by roughly a quarter, to about what you would find on a mountain two and a half kilometres high
source: Own back-of-envelope calculation: conservation of atmospheric mass, US Standard Atmosphere scale height, ETOPO bathymetry. Flagged in the narration as a sketch.

text: Atmospheric water vapour totals about 12,900 cubic kilometres
source: USGS Water Science School, water distribution table

text: Water stays in the atmosphere about nine days on average
source: USGS Water Science School, water cycle: atmosphere

text: About 86 percent of global evaporation comes from the ocean
as_written: about 86 percent of all evaporation on Earth
source: USGS Water Science School, evaporation and the water cycle (about 434,000 of 505,000 cubic km per year)

text: Water vapour and clouds account for about three quarters of the greenhouse effect
source: Schmidt et al. 2010, Journal of Geophysical Research, NASA GISS

text: Earth without a greenhouse effect would average about minus 18 C
source: NASA Climate, 'The Causes of Climate Change' and Earth Observatory

text: The top few metres of ocean hold as much heat as the whole atmosphere
as_written: The top few metres of the sea hold as much heat as the entire atmosphere above it
source: NOAA National Ocean Service

text: Lunar surface reaches about 127 C by day
source: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Diviner instrument

text: Lunar surface falls to about minus 173 C at night
source: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Diviner instrument

text: Record air temperature on Earth is 56.7 C at Death Valley
source: World Meteorological Organization Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (1913)

text: Coldest reliably measured air temperature is minus 89.2 C at Vostok
source: World Meteorological Organization Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (1983)

text: World population exceeds eight billion
as_written: more than eight billion of us
source: United Nations Population Division, World Population Prospects (8 billion reached November 2022)

text: About 40 percent of people live within 100 km of a coast
as_written: About 40 percent live within 100 kilometres of a coast
source: United Nations Atlas of the Oceans

text: About 80 percent of world trade by volume goes by sea
as_written: about 80 percent of world trade by volume
source: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport

text: Aquatic foods supply about 17 percent of animal protein consumed
as_written: about 17 percent of the animal protein
source: FAO, The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2022

text: Glaciers and ice caps hold about 1.7 percent of Earth's water
as_written: about 1.7 percent of all Earth's water
source: USGS Water Science School (1.74 percent)

text: Total living biomass is around 550 gigatonnes of carbon
source: Bar-On, Phillips and Milo 2018, PNAS, 'The biomass distribution on Earth'

text: Plants account for roughly 450 gigatonnes of carbon
source: Bar-On, Phillips and Milo 2018, PNAS

text: Marine biomass is about 6 gigatonnes of carbon, about one percent of the total
as_written: only about 6 gigatonnes. That is about one percent
source: Bar-On, Phillips and Milo 2018, PNAS

text: The ocean produces at least half of atmospheric oxygen, per NOAA; higher figures circulate and are contested
as_written: at least half of the oxygen in the air is produced by the ocean
source: NOAA National Ocean Service, 'How much oxygen comes from the ocean?'

text: Air is about 21 percent oxygen
source: NOAA / NASA atmospheric composition (20.95 percent)

text: Ocean salt spread over land would be roughly 150 m (500 ft) thick
source: NOAA National Ocean Service and USGS, 'Why is the ocean salty' (about 500 feet)

text: The Messinian salinity crisis ran from about 5.97 to 5.33 million years ago
as_written: Between about 5.97 and 5.33 million years ago
source: Manzi et al. 2013 and Krijgsman et al. 1999, Nature, astronomical dating of the Messinian

text: Messinian salt deposits are up to about two kilometres thick
as_written: up to about two kilometres thick
source: Hsu et al. 1973, Deep Sea Drilling Project Leg 13; Ryan 2009

text: Peak Zanclean flood discharge was about 100 million cubic metres per second, hundreds of times the Amazon
as_written: about 100 million cubic metres per second, hundreds of times the flow of the Amazon
source: Garcia-Castellanos et al. 2009, Nature

text: The Mediterranean refilled in between a few months and two years
as_written: somewhere between a few months and two years
source: Garcia-Castellanos et al. 2009, Nature

text: Ground around Hudson Bay rises about one centimetre per year
source: Sella et al. 2007, Geophysical Research Letters, GPS observations of glacial isostatic adjustment

text: Water is about a third as dense as mantle rock, so removing 3.7 km of water implies about a kilometre of rebound (seawater about 1,025 kg per cubic metre, upper mantle about 3,300)
as_written: The floor should rise by roughly a kilometre, over thousands of years
source: Standard Airy isostasy calculation from seawater and upper mantle densities (PREM). Own calculation, flagged as a simple estimate.

text: Tectonic plates move a few centimetres a year
source: USGS, 'Plate tectonics and people'

text: Ringwoodite in a Brazilian diamond contained water, reported in 2014
source: Pearson et al. 2014, Nature; see also Schmandt et al. 2014, Science

text: The Moon recedes about 3.8 cm per year
source: Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector Lunar Laser Ranging; NASA

text: Earth's day lengthens by roughly two milliseconds per century
source: Stephenson, Morrison and Hohenkerk 2016, Proceedings of the Royal Society A; IERS

text: Total lunar tidal dissipation is about 3.7 terawatts
source: Egbert and Ray 2000, Nature

text: Solid Earth tides move the ground by tens of centimetres
source: NOAA National Ocean Service, 'Do tides affect the solid Earth?'

text: Oceans are expected to be lost in roughly a billion years or more as the Sun brightens; timing is debated
as_written: in roughly a billion years or more
source: Wolf and Toon 2015, Science Advances; Ozaki and Reinhard 2021, Nature Geoscience

text: Mars's atmosphere is about 0.6 percent as dense as Earth's
as_written: about 0.6 percent as dense as ours
source: NASA Mars Fact Sheet (mean surface pressure about 636 pascals versus 101,325)
